runs.final_answer:
Assuming your “last Tuesday” means **August 25, 2026** from the date context you supplied:

**Short answer:** I could **not verify any specific public event affecting Project Xanadu on August 25, 2026**. The best-supported reading is that **nothing clearly documented happened that day**, at least in the official Xanadu web presence and readily findable web coverage I could verify.

**Supported fact**
Project Xanadu is an old hypertext project founded in 1960; an incomplete implementation was released in 1998, and OpenXanadu was made available in 2014.  
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Xanadu

**Supported fact**
The current official Project Xanadu homepage is online and shows the page stamp `17.05.07`, which indicates very old front-page material rather than a fresh August 2026 update.  
Source: https://xanadu.com/  
Also: https://www.xanadu.net/

**Supported fact**
A current official demo/instructions page is stamped `16.11.22` and says, “We do not have a product, but a preliminary capability.”  
Source: https://xanadu.com/xuDemoPage.html

**Supported fact**
Another current official page, “The NEW XANADU MODEL FOR THE WEB,” is dated `Jan 1, 2021` and says the new design “is now being written up.”  
Source: https://www.xanadu.net/xuWeb.html

**Supported fact**
The XanaduSpace page says that demo is a “stuck demo,” became “too tangled to improve further,” and that later attempts to refactor it were “beyond fixing.”  
Source: https://xanadu.com/xuspViewer.html

**Supported fact**
Wikipedia’s Project Xanadu page was last edited on **August 13, 2026**, not August 25, 2026.  
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Xanadu

**Inference**
Given those currently available dated pages, I found **no good evidence of a distinct, publicly documented event on August 25, 2026**. What seems to have “happened” to Project Xanadu is not a Tuesday-specific incident, but continued **public stagnation / very low visible activity**.  
Sources informing this inference: https://xanadu.com/ , https://xanadu.com/xuDemoPage.html , https://www.xanadu.net/xuWeb.html , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Xanadu

**Supported fact**
Historically, major reasons for Xanadu’s long failure to ship were a rewrite from C into Smalltalk, a missed Autodesk deadline, Autodesk’s 1992 divestment, and later internal conflict and lack of investment.  
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Xanadu  
Corroborating historical framing: https://web.archive.org/web/20151026021059/https://www.wired.com/1995/06/xanadu/

**Inference**
So if you are asking **why** Project Xanadu appears to be in its present state, the strongest evidence points to **long-term execution problems, rewrites, organizational turmoil, underinvestment, and demos that proved hard to evolve**, not to a single event last Tuesday.  
Sources informing this inference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Xanadu , https://xanadu.com/xuspViewer.html , https://www.xanadu.net/xuWeb.html , https://web.archive.org/web/20151026021059/https://www.wired.com/1995/06/xanadu/

**Disagreement**
The official site presents Project Xanadu as still alive and fighting on (“WE FIGHT ON”).  
Source: https://xanadu.com/

**Disagreement**
Wired historically described Xanadu as “the longest-running vaporware project in the history of computing.”  
Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20151026021059/https://www.wired.com/1995/06/xanadu/

**Uncertainty**
A Xanadu-related site, `xanarama.net`, currently redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page, but I could not verify **when** that happened or whether it is relevant to August 25, 2026 specifically.  
Source URL opened: https://xanarama.net/

**Bottom line**
There is **no solid web evidence I could verify that Project Xanadu had a specific, reportable event on Tuesday, August 25, 2026**. The evidence supports a narrower answer: **Project Xanadu is still online, but its public web presence looks mostly old, sparse, and partially stalled, for long-running structural reasons rather than a clearly documented event last Tuesday.**
